Overview

Leipzig as a Business Centre

Leipzig had 628,718 residents in 2024 according to the city's population register, about 139,000 more than in 2005, which makes it one of the fastest-growing large cities in Germany. Its industrial base is led by vehicle manufacturing: BMW's plant employs about 7,000 people with capacity for up to 350,000 units a year, and Porsche's plant employs about 4,600 and built around 122,000 vehicles in 2023, roughly two thirds of the brand's output. Leipzig/Halle Airport operates around the clock as DHL's largest global hub and the fourth-largest cargo airport in Europe. The city reported record trade tax revenue of 608 million euros in 2023 and 294,324 employees subject to social insurance. Greentech, biotechnology and the digital economy are its three designated clusters.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Leipzig because of the investment and supply chains concentrated in and around it. Automotive and battery plants rely on tiers of suppliers, logistics providers and contractors whose ownership, financial stability and integrity need checking. The airport and surrounding logistics parks move high-value consignments for many shippers, which raises theft, diversion and customs questions. New investors in biotech, greentech and digital companies, and in a rising property market, need diligence on founders and backers. Leipzig is also where the Federal Administrative Court sits and where several criminal senates of the Federal Court of Justice hear appeals, so some significant regulatory and criminal matters reach their final stage in the city.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Leipzig

01

Automotive and battery supplier diligence

Researching suppliers, contractors and logistics partners to vehicle and battery plants in the Leipzig region for ownership, insolvency signals, litigation, sanctions exposure and links to purchasing staff, so manufacturers and tier-one suppliers can make sourcing and onboarding decisions on evidence.

02

Air cargo theft and diversion

Supporting shippers, insurers and their counsel where high-value consignments routed through Leipzig/Halle Airport or nearby logistics parks are lost or diverted, by researching the forwarders, subcontracted carriers and consignees involved and the connections between them.

03

Investor and founder background checks

Reviewing the backgrounds, prior ventures, insolvency history and reputations of founders and investors in Leipzig biotech, greentech and digital companies, using Handelsregister filings, insolvency publications, court decisions and German-language media. This helps investors judge whether claims made in pitch materials hold up.

04

Property and development counterparties

Researching developers, investors and related companies behind Leipzig residential and commercial projects, including shareholder lists, register history, insolvency records and transparency register entries where access is available, to support lenders, buyers and partners in a growing market.

05

Litigation and enforcement support

Supporting counsel in disputes before the Leipzig courts with factual research on counterparties, managing directors and witnesses, and lawful asset research to inform enforcement, including analysis of company histories and related entities registered in Saxony.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Leipzig

Federal courts in Leipzig

The Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht), the highest court of general administrative jurisdiction, has sat at Simsonplatz 1 since moving from Berlin in 2002 and has fourteen senates. The Federal Court of Justice, otherwise based in Karlsruhe, has its 5th and 6th criminal senates in Leipzig, joined by a new 7th criminal senate from 1 July 2026, housed at the Villa Sack on Karl-Heine-Straße.

Leipzig register court

The Amtsgericht Leipzig, at Bernhard-Göring-Straße 64, keeps the commercial register for the Leipzig regional court district, covering the city of Leipzig, the Landkreis Leipzig and Landkreis Nordsachsen, together with the partnership, cooperative and association registers. Entries and filed documents, including GmbH shareholder lists, are accessible through the joint register portal of the German states. Annual financial statements are published separately through the company register.

Saxony as the regulatory setting

Leipzig sits in the Free State of Saxony, whose courts hear first-instance civil, commercial and criminal matters arising in the city. Germany has no dedicated licensing regime for private investigators, so activity in Leipzig is governed by federal trade, data protection, criminal and civil law, with Saxony's data protection authority supervising private-sector processing in the state. Employee investigations must also respect works council rights.

Airport logistics cluster

Leipzig/Halle Airport is a 24-hour cargo airport and DHL's largest global hub, ranked fourth among European cargo airports. The surrounding logistics and distribution sites handle express, e-commerce and industrial freight for many shippers and carriers, so loss and diversion inquiries typically involve several subcontracted parties and records held in more than one country. Records from airline, handler and forwarder systems may need to be requested through counsel.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Leipzig

TDSC handles Leipzig matters from Nashville and has no office or staff in Germany. Engagements begin with the decision or dispute at issue and then map lawful sources: the Handelsregister and filed documents via the joint register portal, insolvency publications, court decisions, the transparency register where access applies, land register information where a legitimate interest can be shown through counsel, sanctions lists and German-language media. Where interviews, site visits or observation in Leipzig or Saxony are needed, TDSC coordinates experienced German investigators and agrees methods with the client's German counsel, within the GDPR, the Federal Data Protection Act and works council rules for employee matters. Reports separate documented facts from inference.

TDSC has no office in Leipzig. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Leipzig: Frequently Asked Questions

Where are Leipzig companies registered?

Companies seated in Leipzig, the Landkreis Leipzig and Landkreis Nordsachsen are entered in the commercial register kept by the Amtsgericht Leipzig. Entries and filed documents, including articles and GmbH shareholder lists, can be retrieved through the joint register portal of the German states, which TDSC uses alongside insolvency publications and court decisions.

Can you vet suppliers to the BMW or Porsche plants in Leipzig?

TDSC can research a supplier's ownership, managing directors, financial filings, insolvency signals, litigation, sanctions exposure and links to purchasing staff, for a manufacturer or tier-one supplier that is the client. TDSC does not act for or on behalf of the carmakers unless engaged by them, and works only from lawful sources.

Which federal courts sit in Leipzig?

The Federal Administrative Court sits at Simsonplatz 1 and is the highest court of general administrative jurisdiction. The Federal Court of Justice has its 5th, 6th and, from July 2026, 7th criminal senates in Leipzig. Civil and commercial cases from the city start in the Saxon courts.

Does TDSC have investigators in Leipzig?

No. TDSC has no office or staff in Germany. Public-record and open-source research is carried out from Nashville, and where field work in Leipzig or Saxony is needed TDSC coordinates experienced German investigators working under a written scope and within German data protection and other applicable law.

Can you help with a shipment lost via Leipzig/Halle Airport?

TDSC researches the forwarders, subcontracted carriers, warehouses and consignees in the chain, their ownership, histories and connections, and any prior claims or insolvency, to help insurers and counsel understand how a loss occurred and who may be liable. Physical inspection and interviews are coordinated with appropriate German professionals.
